Testing three of the six objects does that:
- **If the machine needs one nexiom:** it lights when at least one nexiom is in the set. That covers 12 of the 15 pairs.
- **If the machine needs two nexioms:** it lights only when both nexioms are in the set. That covers 3 of the 15 pairs.

So 15 of the 30 hypotheses predict a light and 15 predict no light, an even split.

- **Needs two:** any pair is possible except the 3 pairs drawn entirely from nedupon, letesi and vipevar. That leaves 12 pairs.

Testing teseluk, fotesen, nedupon and letesi splits these about evenly:
- **Needs one:** all 3 remaining pairs include teseluk or fotesen, so all 3 would light.
- **Needs two:** the four objects form 6 pairs. Nedupon+letesi is already ruled out, so 5 of these would light.

That is 8 hypotheses predicting a light and 7 predicting no light.

TEST: teseluk, fotesen, nedupon, letesi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

After two failed tests, "needs one" is ruled out entirely. Under that rule, both nexioms would have to be among teseluk, fotesen and tanesil. Every such pair includes teseluk or fotesen, so the second test would have lit up. **The machine needs two nexioms together.**

Seven pairs remain possible: nedupon+tanesil, letesi+tanesil, vipevar+teseluk, vipevar+fotesen, vipevar+tanesil, teseluk+tanesil, fotesen+tanesil.

Two tests give at most 4 outcomes, so I can't guarantee singling out one pair from 7. I'll split them as evenly as I can. Testing vipevar, teseluk and tanesil lights only for 3 pairs (vipevar+teseluk, vipevar+tanesil, teseluk+tanesil), leaving 4 that wouldn't.

TEST: vipevar, teseluk, tanesil
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up, so the nexioms are one of three pairs: vipevar+teseluk, vipevar+tanesil, or teseluk+tanesil.

One yes/no test can't separate three options for certain. Testing vipevar and teseluk together lights only if that is the pair. If it lights, I'm done. If not, I'll have to pick between the other two.

TEST: vipevar, teseluk
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test ruled out vipevar+teseluk. That leaves two pairs: **vipevar+tanesil** or **teseluk+tanesil**.

Nothing I've seen favours either, so this answer is a guess with a 50% chance of being right. Tanesil is certainly a nexiom. The machine definitely **needs two** nexioms, because the second test ruled out "needs one."

ANSWER: nexioms = vipevar, tanesil; needs = two
